segments.he: מַתְנִי׳ עֲגָלָה שֶׁל קָטָן — טְמֵאָה מִדְרָס, וְנִטֶּלֶת בְּשַׁבָּת, וְאֵינָהּ נִגְרֶרֶת אֶלָּא עַל גַּבֵּי כֵלִים.
segments.en: «MISHNA:» «A child’s wagon,» with which he plays and upon which he also sits, «is susceptible to ritual impurity» imparted by «treading.» It is considered a fixed seat of the child, so that if the child is a zav and he sits on the wagon, it contracts the ritual impurity imparted by the treading of a zav. «And» this wagon «may be handled on Shabbat,» as it is considered a vessel. «And it may be dragged» on the ground on Shabbat «only upon cloth,» a stone pavement, or the like, as otherwise it would create a furrow when dragged, and one would be liable due to the prohibited labor of plowing.

segments.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: כׇּל הַכֵּלִים אֵין נִגְרָרִין, חוּץ מִן הָעֲגָלָה, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהִיא כּוֹבֶשֶׁת.
segments.en: «Rabbi Yehuda says:» For this reason, «no vessels may be dragged» on the ground on Shabbat «except for a wagon,» which is permitted «because» its wheels do not make a furrow in the ground but merely «press» the earth down. Since no earth is moved from its place, this is not considered digging or plowing on Shabbat.
